references.text: Earlier in the same chapter, God warned the people to set boundaries around the mountain so that no one would touch it. This verse repeats the warning.
God repeats the warning to Moses that neither the people nor the priests should break through to come up to the Lord.
God tells Moses that no one can see his face and live. This underscores the danger of seeing God.
The Kohathites were warned not to go in and look at the holy things, not even for a moment, or they would die. The same principle regarding the danger of holiness applies here.
The Lord struck down men from Beth-Shemesh because they looked into the ark of the Lord. This shows the consequence of looking upon the holy without permission.
The book of Hebrews refers to the events at Mount Sinai and the terrifying revelation that the people could not endure.
The repetition of 'go down' linked with the people's sin and the danger of God's presence creates a clear narrative parallel.
Direct continuity: 20:20 explains the theology behind the warning in 19:21 regarding God's holy presence.
Contrast between Moses' ability to avert judgment at Sinai (Ex 19) and his powerlessness in Jeremiah's time (Jer 15).
